_readme: Creator Marketing and Partnerships, Version 1.1: the page's words and its media configuration, section by section (src/pages/work/creator-campaigns.astro and src/components/creator/). Version 1.1 is John's delta brief (October 2026) against the deployed Version 1.0: the hero headline and paragraph, the program context, the creator network's introduction and handles (no destinations on the creators), the atlas sublines and content counts, the Mykonos co-sponsor, the Trezor Dare Ad and its three creator-account highlights, the selected-content library (six formats, one edit each), the program ownership in three chapters, the credit stack and the conclusion, word for word; everything else is Version 1.0 (the approved copy and the confirmed roster and affiliations). A field set to null is a placeholder: it shows as a labeled placeholder in `npm run dev` only and renders nothing in a production build, so the public page never shows one (testimonials, Trezor's assignment, objective and approach, the Trezor collaboration rows without names, the creators' category labels). Media slots name asset ids in src/data/assets.json; every slot already holds its final aspect ratio, all of them square or landscape.

hero._hero: 05 Hero: one full-screen landscape composition in layers (the coastal-estate reference, used for the hero only): the sky, the headline, the villa and its palms in front of the headline's lower line, and two palm fronds at the corners, each moving at its own rate as the page scrolls, with a slow drift of their own; reduced motion holds the layers still. The photographs are illustrative stock (Unsplash), credited once, in the credits (V1.1), and never presented as footage from the trips.
hero.label: 01 / Creator Marketing and Partnerships
hero.headline: Creator campaigns, built to travel.
hero.copy: I helped lead creator programs across Costa Rica, Singapore, and Mykonos, owning campaign strategy, creative direction, sponsor coordination, on-site production, and distribution in close collaboration with Maanav Porwal and Bob van der Meer.

context._context: 06 Program context: John's V1.1 headline (its second sentence in the accent) and one paragraph that names his primary ownership and credits Maanav Porwal's and Bob van der Meer's collaboration (no services grid), with a single drawn route that leaves the paragraph and leads into the creator network.
context.headline: A trip is the setting. A program connects everything around it.
context.accent: A program connects everything around it.
context.copy: For Bolt Liquidity, each trip brought creators, sponsors, and a production plan together for a few focused days. My primary ownership covered campaign strategy with co-sponsors, sponsor coordination, creative direction, on-site shoot planning, approvals, distribution, and reporting. Maanav Porwal collaborated on creator and co-sponsor sourcing, negotiations, contracts, travel, and logistics, while Bob van der Meer collaborated on concepts and handled much of the filming and editing.

network._network: 07 Creator network: exactly the eight creators John confirmed, each with a display name and handle (V1.1), square profile pictures traveling one way, slowly, around a curved path in depth, with no controls and nothing to drag. Hovering, focusing or selecting a creator shows their name, handle and confirmed affiliations at the center; nothing on the cards is a testimonial, a follower count, a ranking or a destination history. Reduced motion holds the ring still; narrow screens show a plain list with everything visible. Handles are plain text, not links. `category` is a placeholder label (null until John confirms one).
network.headline: The creators who made it travel.
network.sub: Eight creators spanning streaming, crypto media, ecosystem leadership, entertainment, and community.

creators.name: The Blonde Broker
affiliations: VP of Financial Services at Corgi

voices._voices: 08 The testimonial transition: up to three short creator testimonials (one or two sentences each), one at a time as the page scrolls, lower left, lower right, then lower left again on the way into the destinations, each with its attribution. They are V1 placeholders (assets.json, pending): until one is approved the section renders nothing in a production build and the network leads straight into the atlas. Never on the creator cards, and never Trezor's feedback, which belongs to the Trezor section.

atlas._atlas: 09 Campaign atlas: one stage that holds still while the reader scrolls through three states, Costa Rica, Singapore and Mykonos, each with its own loop (5 to 10 seconds, silent, landscape, reset with a dissolve), two fragments, color atmosphere, large name, chapter index and concise copy. Wide screens with motion allowed pin it; narrow or short screens, reduced motion and no JavaScript show the three chapters one after another. Counts: creators as the V1.0 roster counted them (6, 7 and 4), content pieces as John gave them in V1.1 (40+, 35+ and 25+). `sponsors` names logo ids in src/data/logos.json.
atlas.title: Three destinations, one program.

destinations.name: Costa Rica
destinations.copy: A creator house on the Pacific coast where shared moments became destination content, creator-led integrations, and bespoke campaigns produced for co-sponsors.

destinations.name: Singapore
destinations.copy: A crypto game show on a party bus, high tea on the 56th floor, and a shopping spree through the city's luxury malls, designed as a conference activation.

destinations.name: Mykonos
destinations.copy: A villa above the Aegean, a day on a catamaran, and long dinners into the evening, with four creators turning each moment into content.

trezor._trezor: 10 Trezor Dare Ad: the final video first (Trezor Dare Ad.mp4, with sound, on request), then the assignment, the objective and the approach (placeholders until John supplies them), three performance highlights from the creator's own account (compared with that account's preceding three months, never presented as Trezor's total campaign performance), Trezor's feedback (one concise attributed quote, kept apart from the creator testimonials) and the collaboration credits.
trezor.title: Trezor Dare Ad
trezor.deck: A creator-led sponsor integration for Trezor, filmed at the creator house in Costa Rica.
trezor.metricsNote: Measured on the creator's own account against that account's preceding three months. These are creator-account results, not Trezor's total campaign performance.

library._library: 11 Selected content: a library of six edits from across the three trips, one per format, each a curated mini-edit of its own (silent, landscape, 9 to 12 seconds), chosen with simple text tabs and a restrained active line that fills as the edit plays. Selecting a format plays its edit from the start; with motion allowed the library moves on to the next format when an edit ends, the reader can pause it at any time, and it holds while keyboard focus is in the formats. Reduced motion, a data-saving preference or a refused autoplay start nothing: the selected edit waits on its poster and plays on request. Without JavaScript the six edits read in turn, each with its own controls. `cues` are the edit's own times (seconds) where each destination takes over, for the place line under the frame.
library.headline: One program, many formats.
library.copy: Choose a format to watch its edit, drawn from across the three trips.
library.label: Formats

ownership._ownership: 12 Program ownership: John's working headline, its first sentence above a waterline and its second below it, where three editorial chapters (V1.1) set out how the program was built, directed and carried to market, each crediting who owned it: no list of areas, no rings, no cards or pills.
ownership.headline: The experience was visible. The system behind it was not.
ownership.below: The system behind it was not.
ownership.copy: Beneath every post was a collaborative program spanning sourcing, logistics, creative direction, production, distribution, and partner reporting.

credits._credits: 13 Credits: one system for everyone who made the work, set like a film's closing credits. The team first (V1.1): John Cowin, Maanav Porwal and Bob van der Meer, each with what they owned or collaborated on, word for word from John's brief; then the eight creators, the co-sponsors, the brand and the hero's illustrative photography (credited here only). Nothing implies John edited, shot or designed the work.
credits.title: Many hands, one program.

conclusion._conclusion: 14 The conclusion: one short idea (the program kept working after each trip), then the way on to the next case study in order (Technical Product Marketing), then the shared Contact section.
conclusion.headline: The trip ends. The program keeps working.
conclusion.copy: Each activation produced an immediate body of campaign content and strengthened the creator and partner relationships behind the next opportunity. The value continued through distribution, reporting, and ongoing collaboration after everyone went home.
conclusion.nextLine: Next, see how I turn technical complexity into a clear market narrative.
